style: Gritty late-90s New York street rap, dusty sampled breakbeat, 90 BPM, unhurried countdown. Mood: a frozen city block at 3 a.m. in 1997, streetlight hum, nobody trusts anybody, tense and sly. Sample: a dark half-second horn hit layered on minor-key strings, cut from an old soul record, firing once on each number and then going silent. Drums: fat thumping kick, hard rimshot-bright snare, loose shuffled hats, warm low bass, vinyl hiss. Voice: young male tenor, high, nasal, a little raspy, bold corner bark, punchy and on the grid but relaxed; he calls the number, pauses a beat, then raps the rule. Wordless DJ scratch fills between rules. Final line over drums alone.
exclude: sung chorus, melodic singing, choir, autotune, trap hats, 808 slides, EDM drop, double-time flow, rushed delivery, female vocals, crowd chant, spoken-word poetry
lyrics:
[Intro: single horn-and-strings hit, then kick and snare drop in; cold, sly]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Instrumental break: DJ scratch fill, no vocals]

[Verse: punchy, deliberate, one bar per line; the number alone, a breath, then the rule]
[horn stab]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Instrumental break: chirp scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Instrumental break: scratch cut, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Instrumental break: chirp scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Instrumental break: scratch cut, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Instrumental break: short scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Instrumental break: dragged scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab, quieter, voice drops low]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Instrumental break: chirp scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Instrumental break: stutter scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab, knowing, a little smirk]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Instrumental break: double scratch, no vocals]

[horn stab, loudest of all]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro: sample and bass drop out, drums only; plain, slow]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
title: tec-all10-B-street-tenor-horn-stabs
